    Friday 25 September 2026

    Morning briefing

    Morning briefing

    The room switches to one number per option row with no break on any of sixteen sheets, the Decoder abstains on all forty lines, and the chair ships a short, one-bet book - three option legs and five tech longs against five shorts, every line tied inside its tier - while the desk brief shows the slate itself is a volume-ratio sort

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). Overnight: Asia closed split, the Nikkei 225 up 1.30% against the Hang Seng down 1.01% with Shanghai and KOSPI stale (QUOTED=executive.user.txt); Europe is up in session, DAX +0.59% and Euro Stoxx 50 +0.52% (QUOTED=executive.user.txt); the futures were bid, S&P +0.33% and Nasdaq-100 +0.48% (QUOTED=executive.user.txt), yet SPY sat at -0.06% by the 10:06 market stamp (QUOTED=executive.user.txt), so the open's bid was already being handed back before the freeze. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims - Europe and the futures agree while Asia disagrees with itself, which is the configuration that most often retraces, and I expect the index to climb back through the morning level into the close; a QQQ close under its level at the 10:08 freeze (QUOTED=desk_brief.txt) means the shape failed. The regime is mixed: SPY flat on the week at +0.66%, QQQ up +2.89%, IWM down -1.26%, VIX 15.18 on a rising five-day trend and the ten-year at 5.19 and rising (QUOTED=executive.user.txt). The book's conviction is ONE bet, long large-cap tech and semis into a QQQ-up tape: the five share longs (MSFT, QCOM, TXN, COST, CDNS), the SMCI call and the GOOGL call are that single bet, SMCI's call is its best expression because it carries the cheapest reach on the sheet, and the five share shorts (CHTR, GS, SCHW, BX, MCD) and the ABNB put are offsets that cut variance, not a second source of mean. What invalidates the top ideas is a QQQ close under the freeze level today and, for the two calls, Monday's US-China trade details on 2026-09-28 (QUOTED=executive.user.txt) landing badly on chips. R72 (QUOTED=executive.user.txt): the flat ten is five longs against five shorts and earns only the spread between them, while my top five is the five longs - it adds the index's move from the freeze to the close, so it beats the flat ten tonight only if the retrace-then-reclaim shape prints and loses to it if the index closes under the freeze, and that is the whole of my ordering's claim. Under R35 and R78 (QUOTED=executive.user.txt) no instrument authors a departure, so every share line sits within eight points of the one-median, and under my own tie rule the only spread I sign is the long tier at 53 over everything else at 42, with the option column tied at 46 (COUNTED=json.load(grades/executive.json) leads[].final_grade). The pyramid leader is the Black Swan, and its read diverges from the room exactly on my shorts: it grades linear share shorts near the floor (CHTR 12 against a room median of 50) and prefers the capped-loss contracts (ABNB put 47 against 46) (QUOTED=executive.user.txt); under R33 (QUOTED=executive.user.txt) it carries no extra weight. The chair-served model agrees with the room on SMCI (+8.44%) and QCOM (+4.12%) and disagrees sharply on AMP (-4.17% on a long the room grades 48) (QUOTED=executive.user.txt); with no ledger record it moves no grade. Horizon split: intraday 5, swing 28, position 6, long_term 1 (COUNTED=Counter(leads[].horizon_class) over grades/executive.json). HOUSE RULES: every share line at share_default 1.0 and every option leg at option_default 0.6, no line at the 1.5 per-line cap, no overrides and no vacancies (COUNTED=columns.json stakes); share lines are scored at today's close and killed only by their close-based level at the next open; option legs settle at the first of the ratchet close, the kill close, or the close of 2026-10-01 for SMCI and GOOGL and 2026-10-15 for ABNB (COUNTED=last session before each served expiry); windfall policy - a leg that closes through its ratchet is banked whole, with no re-entry, no adds and no averaging down, and nothing in this book changes mid-session.

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: FIFTEEN graders - the Decoder in its second session - then the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 10:08 ET, WITH 351 MINUTES OF TAPE LEFT BEFORE THE CLOSE: every entry is an early-afternoon mark, not an open, and under R14 a window that short makes seat ranks advisory.

    NOTHING HERE CAME FROM THE APP'S MOCK PATH. Run 47 is the only book of 2026-09-25 and it shipped on the first attempt.

Seats extract their candidate tables to work on them, and this session gave them no per-seat folder: 49 files were written there during the board, several under the same generic names (cands.txt, cands.json, build.py, check.py, dump.py). Flow reported reading another seat's extract - it carried a technicals field Flow's prompt does not serve - before re-extracting privately and grading from its own prompt. No other seat reported it, and the files alone cannot rule a cross-read out; value_grep cannot see one where the figure is also in the reading seat's prompt. From the next session each seat works in a private folder and is barred from every other scratch file.
